kf: In skin of colour, **post-inflammatory hyperpigmentation** and flexural darkening are everyday problems; true **depigmentation** (vitiligo, piebaldism) is separate.
Treat the driver of PIH (acne, eczema, shaving friction); daily tinted broad-spectrum sunscreen; azelaic acid.
Warn about **unlicensed bleaching creams** (mercury, potent steroids, high-strength hydroquinone).
Piebaldism is congenital and stable (white forelock); vitiligo is acquired and autoimmune.
Pale patches: think pityriasis alba, PIH (hypo), pityriasis versicolor, PMH, vitiligo, leprosy (numb).
myths: **"Bleaching creams are safe cosmetics"**: illegal products cause steroid damage, ochronosis and mercury toxicity.
patho_lead: Pigment change after inflammation depends on **where the melanin ends up**.

mech.t: Inflamed melanocytes over-produce pigment in the epidermis: brown, fades in months.
Basal damage drops pigment into the dermis: grey-blue, slow to fade.
mech.cap: Pigment incontinence makes deeper, greyer pigment.

mech.t: Inflammation may reduce melanin transfer, leaving pale areas.
Absent melanocytes (vitiligo, piebaldism) give chalk-white skin.

comp: Psychological impact; harm from bleaching products.
prog: PIH fades over months to years if the trigger stops.
